top_changes.change: Replace the live/restored current decals (dashed white lane lines and chevrons that read as road markings) with a flow-foam/ripple surface treatment that follows the channel and visibly calms on restoration, plus a restored-state colour/sandbar change

Rebuild Veilfall as a monumental hero landmark: stacked green-capped cliffs with several broad white falls, base spray and an arch entrance per the stronghold board, replacing the dark rectangular tower with one thin streak

Fight presentation cleanup: swap the flat sprawling magenta ellipses for grounded terrain-conforming telegraphs, remove raw debug strings (combat_char..., combat_quick...) and overlapping prompt text, texture the flat gray cliff and soften the hard tiled grass/sand edge in the Venn arena

rows.reason: Islands now read as pale warm dune sand with foam-ringed shallows instead of grassy domes on gray skirts, but the dunes are smooth uniform mounds with sparse grass tufts, little damp-edge darkening or sheltered shrub pockets, so shore ecology is still thin.

Mosshell idle, moving and hurt are effectively the same silhouette, and Cannonback/Aquaryn hurt and moving differ only slightly from idle; Ripplet hurt shows a small hunch but states still need the filename to read.
The map canvas is a black rectangle with a single position marker and 'Surveyed: 0%'; no terrain, coastline, islands or roads are drawn.

Six of thirteen shinies (Abyssal Guardian, Cragclaw, Mangrove Monitor, Riverdrake, Sirenseal, Torrentoad) are flat saturated hot magenta blobs with no pattern or material identity; Mosshell, Ripplet, Tidecoil and Cannonback shinies keep their species read.
No ground pickups are shown at normal camera distance in these sheets.

Veilfall reads as a dark near-rectangular rock tower with one thin straight white streak at distance; the close S3 view shows a wider fall against faceted gray rock but no green tiers, multiple cascades, arch or base spray from the stronghold board.
The only visible destinations are a small white stone arch, a white dome hut and a small beacon on open sand at First Shore; no distinct halls, terraces or lived-in docks are visible.

The trainer is upright in the water with both arms raised straight overhead and boots visible beneath the surface in every swim frame, reading as wading or waving for help rather than a horizontal surface stroke.

Tidecoil, Riverdrake, Sirenseal, Aquaryn and Mangrove Monitor now lie flat on the ground, but Ripplet still sits in an alert crouch with head raised, Torrentoad faints belly-up, and fainted Cannonback turns bleached white.

Every tab is the same dark translucent slate panel with thin borders and small gray text over a dimmed world; the Creatures page has a model render, but headers, focus and gold progression accents are weak so hierarchy is flat.
Build now shows three illustrated cards (Tent, Campfire, Bedroll) and Save lists five slots, but Quests and Players remain a few thin rows with most of the panel empty.
Named Tidewake characters are not identifiable in these frames; only the trainer, a hatted guide and a few tiny HUD-scene NPCs appear.

Water now grades from pale turquoise shallows and foam-ringed sandbars to deep navy offshore with visible ripples, though the sea is still a fairly uniform plane without reef, kelp or depth-varying features.
Tells are huge flat pink/magenta ellipses sprawling across the arena plus text banners ('incoming - move', 'HEAVY - get clear'); hit frames show only a thin pink line and no impact silhouette.
No catching frames are included.
The fight sheets show Ripplet against Cannonback; no Riverdrake fight frames are present.
The centre of the view is open, but there are still about eight separate dark boxes (clock, location, main story, minimap, team, hotbar, key prompts, health/food) spread around the edges.
A white foam ring now surrounds the swimmer and no hard shadow sits beside the body, but there is no trailing wake or splash, so motion through the water does not read.
No candy pickups are shown.
The team roster now sits on a dark backed panel with green bars and stays legible over grass and sand, though its portraits and bars are tiny.
No partly buried blue figure is visible behind Ripplet; the only background figure is a small standing humanoid grounded on the sand.
The shallows ahead are a row of near-identical oval pale sandbars with matching foam rims spaced evenly in a line, which still reads as a manufactured stepping-stone chain.
Quick bindings is a clean table with pad and key columns, but Controls still opens with a dense gray paragraph and small literal labels ('Left stick up', 'W') with no button glyphs.
Live currents are drawn as bright white dashed lane lines bordering a lighter strip with chevron arrows, literally reading like road markings painted on the sea; t0 and t1 are nearly identical.
Restored states only fade the lane strip and dim the dashes, which remain visible; water colour, sandbars and surrounding geometry are unchanged.
No dialogue frames are included.
The TIDEWAKE heading matches the boxed, highlighted Tidewake tab while Meadows is plain.
No catch result frames are included.
No dialogue frames are included.
Riptusk's resting pose still rolls onto its side/back with pale belly up and limbs splayed, reading distressed; Torrentoad has no resting frame and its fainted frame is also belly-up.
No flying frames are included.
Ripplet and Cannonback stay mostly side by side without head overlap, but in several frames the trainer stands directly against Ripplet's body and the two creatures touch at the attack line.
The boss title card now sits in the upper right and never covers Cannonback's shell or head.
Named characters are not shown, but at the Salt Crown camp dense uniform pale-green grass reaches the trainer's knees and hides the legs and camp pieces.

No Riverdrake fight win frames are included.
Aquaryn stands tall and upright on its legs on the water surface with the rider perched high, identical across frames 08-10, with no wake, splash, bob or stroke.

The creature bed is still a flat speckled orange-brown oval in a dark raised curb, and at Salt Crown it reads as a thin strip edge-on; there is no bedding volume.
